|---|---|---|
| package purge fails once (each OS family) | package still installed, hold and `client.keys` gone, registration removed, writer released | preview lists the host as skewed; the reruns finish both hosts |
| `auditd` restart fails after the purge | no package, audit plugin still listening: shown as a `residue` row in the preview | rerun only retires the plugin; verify 16/16 pass. A control host with stale `client.keys` and no listener was not selected and left untouched |
| controller killed with `SIGKILL` during the purge | `writer-active.json` remains, package still installed | next run refuses, naming the marker; after the runbook's checks (nothing running; component `agent`, mode `apply`, owner of 32 hex digits) the marker was removed by hand and the rerun removed both hosts |

The `SIGKILL` arm was executed four times. In the first execution the rerun after the manual marker removal
stopped on `wsk-deb` (package left installed, `client.keys` gone, hold released, registration removed: the
state of the purge-failure row above); its full output was not kept and the cause is not known. The next
three executions (with the rerun's output kept) finished both hosts with `failed=0`. A rerun of the failed
state is the resumability claim covered by the purge-failure row, but the one failure was not explained.

**Tag-scoped direct runs.** `--tags C7` on all hosts: claims and releases the writer on the two skewed hosts,
nothing else changes (`changed=1` is the read-only `group_by` bookkeeping task), no marker left, `wsk-ok`
untouched. `--tags C6 --limit wsk-deb`: the agent is stopped and disabled and removed from the manager, the
package, hold and `client.keys` remain, the result line says `would-remove`; the next full run lists
`wsk-deb` again and finishes it.

**Interactive terminal (real PTY).** `pilot hotfix wazuh-agent-skew` without `--force`, driven through its
prompts (inventory, secrets answered No, sudo answered No, stage sandbox): the confirmation defaults to No;
pressing Enter printed "已取消，沒有變更任何東西。", exit 0, every host unchanged. A second run answering Yes
removed `wsk-deb` and `wsk-el`, left `wsk-ok`, exit 0.

**Secrets.** The three agent keys from the fixture were searched (fixed-string) in every raw output of these
arms and in this record: 0 hits.

Natural faults on this candidate (not injected): the fixture ran clean on its first attempt. An extra
`wazuh-fim-apply.yml` run on the AlmaLinux host, started before the skew step as a precaution, was refused by
its own version gate ("installed Wazuh agent is newer than the observed manager"), because the fixture had
already produced the skew; this is the refusal the hotfix exists for. The `SIGKILL` arm's one unexplained
rerun failure is described above. The existing who-data restart race tracked in #330 did not occur on this
candidate.

## Not covered / limits (fill in)

- Ubuntu 24.04 and AlmaLinux 9.8 only; Ubuntu 22.04 and other EL releases were not run.
- One `wazuh-manager` host; a `prod` run was not executed on a host (the prod attestation refusal was
  exercised, the approval path is covered by static tests of the playbook); `--stage staging` was run only
  with an inventory in which the manager is also in `staging`.
- The skew was produced by replacing the package outside pilot (fixture), not by a natural upgrade.
- Interruption was exercised at three points (purge failure, `auditd` restart failure, `SIGKILL` during the
  purge). A run killed between other steps, and a package manager killed while it holds its own lock, were
  not run; the runbook documents the marker recovery but the failure of the package manager itself is left
  to the operator. One rerun failure in the `SIGKILL` arm was not explained (see above).
- The EL redeploy can still fail once because of the #330 who-data race, independent of this change.
- `wazuh-agent-hotfix.py` was exercised through Ansible on real hosts; its refusal branches for a malformed
  `client.keys`, a symlinked `client.keys` or policy path, unsafe ownership, an unknown package state or
  architecture, a manager group with zero or two hosts, an unreadable or non-4.14.x manager version, and the
  `pilot_hotfix_deregister=false` diagnostic are covered by unit controls only; `--timeout` expiry and the
  vault or become password prompts' Yes paths were not run.
- The spec's C6 row is strict only on a host that runs the manager stack and vacuous elsewhere; it was
  verified on `wsk-manager` only, and only through `pilot verify --local` (see #332 for why the shape of
  that matcher matters).
- The faults were produced with shims or by hand on disposable VMs (marked in the arms above); a real
  package-manager failure was not waited for.
- The run's `ansible-playbook` was ansible-core 2.19.2; CI installs the newest 2.19.x (2.19.15 when this
  record was written), against which only the Go playbook harness tests were run, not these target arms.
